# update: docker: exit with 1 without any message

Make `self-update docker` succeed when there is nothing to do:

```bash
$ images all
# nothing
$ self-update docker || echo $?
# echo 1
```

With no images, the `docker images … | xargs -n1 docker pull` pipeline ran `docker pull` with no argument (or `xargs` returned non-zero), the script — under `set -e` — exited 1 before printing anything, and the remaining update steps were skipped.
